findings.description: send_email() and send_email_with_attachments() are async fns but use the synchronous SmtpTransport built by create_transport() (line 76) and its blocking .send() method (lines 352, 405, 453). Each call blocks a tokio executor thread for the entire SMTP round-trip, stalling other tasks on that worker thread. Line 280 correctly uses the async transport; the other three do not.
findings.fix: Replace the blocking calls with the async transport: change create_transport() usage in send_email()/send_email_with_attachments() to create_async_transport() (which already exists at line ~100) and call transport.send(email_msg).await. Alternatively wrap the sync send in tokio::task::spawn_blocking. Delete create_transport() once unused.

findings.description: get_teable_config() calls Config::from_env() which re-reads all environment variables on EVERY Teable API call (member lookup, work-hour CRUD, paginated fetches). This is the same per-request config reload that was fixed for JWT in PR #35, but the Teable path was left behind.
findings.fix: Build TeableConfig once at startup: construct it in main() from the already-loaded Config, add a 'teable_config: TeableConfig' field to AppState (make TeableConfig pub and Clone), pass &state.teable_config into every teable.rs function instead of calling get_teable_config() internally. Then delete get_teable_config().

findings.description: reset_password() first calls is_token_valid() (token_store.rs:83, read lock, checks expiry) and then consume_reset_token() (token_store.rs:71, write lock, does NOT check expiry). Two lock acquisitions create a time-of-check/time-of-use window: a token can expire between the check and the consume, and consume_reset_token would happily return an expired token.
findings.fix: Replace the two methods with a single atomic method on TokenStore: 'pub async fn consume_valid_reset_token(&self, token: &str) -> Option<ResetToken>' that acquires the write lock once, removes the token, and returns it only if expires_at > Utc::now() (re-inserting or discarding if expired). Update routes/auth.rs:263-272 to call only this method. Remove is_token_valid() or mark it for tests only.

findings.description: The CREATE TABLE reset_tokens migration (lines 45-58) still runs at every startup, but all reset-token SQL methods were deleted in PR #35 and the app uses the in-memory TokenStore instead. The table is dead schema.
findings.fix: Delete the second sqlx::query(...) block creating the reset_tokens table (lines 45-58) from Database::new(). Existing databases keep the orphaned table harmlessly; optionally document a manual DROP TABLE for operators.

findings.description: The multipart form-parsing loop (fields: subject, message, include_greeting, plus attachment collection with MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE check) is duplicated almost verbatim between send_test_mail() (lines 78-125, loop at 85) and send_bulk_mail() (lines 215-266, loop at 224). A diff shows only ~6 lines differ (recipient_filter field).
findings.fix: Extract a helper: 'async fn parse_mail_multipart(multipart: &mut Multipart) -> Result<MailForm, Response>' returning a struct MailForm { subject, message, include_greeting, attachments, recipient_filter: Option<String> }. Both handlers call it; send_bulk_mail additionally validates recipient_filter.

findings.description: The ownership-verification pattern (fetch work hour by id, extract member id via wh.get_member_id(), compare to current user, return identical 'not found or no permission' JSON) is duplicated between get_work_hour_by_id() (lines 109-122) and update_work_hour() (lines 395-408), and partially reimplemented a third way in delete_work_hour() (lines ~476-485).
findings.fix: Extract one helper: 'async fn verify_work_hour_ownership(client: &Client, work_hour_id: &str, user_id: &str) -> Result<WorkHour, Response>' that fetches the record, checks ownership, and returns the WorkHour or the exact error response. Call it from all three handlers.

findings.description: The orga-role authorization (check claims.role from JWT, fetch member record, double-check member.has_role("orga"), return 403/404) is duplicated between send_test_mail() (lines 55-67) and send_bulk_mail() (lines 186-213).
findings.fix: Extract 'async fn require_orga_role(state: &AppState, claims: &AuthClaims) -> Result<Member, StatusCode>' that performs the member fetch and both role checks, returning the Member on success. Both handlers call it.

findings.description: main() creates a dedicated 'check_client = Client::new()' for the startup diagnostics, then creates a second Client::new() for AppState.http_client a few lines later. Two identical HTTP clients for the same process.
findings.fix: Create one reqwest::Client before the diagnostics, clone it (Client is cheap to clone, shares the connection pool) for both the check_table_access calls and AppState.http_client.

findings.description: 'pub use state::*;' re-exports everything from the state module at crate root 'for tests', making items visible through two paths and pulling unrelated items (middleware, extractors) into the root namespace.
findings.fix: Delete line 35. In the test module, import explicitly what is used: 'use crate::state::{self, AppState};' (most tests already reach items via state::AppState, so likely only removing the glob is needed plus adding explicit imports where compilation fails).

findings.description: check_table_access() returns Result<u64, String> - stringly-typed errors that cannot be matched, chained, or enriched with context, unlike the rest of the crate which now uses anyhow.
findings.fix: Change the signature to 'pub async fn check_table_access(...) -> anyhow::Result<u64>' and replace the format!()-built Err strings with anyhow::anyhow!(...) (optionally with .context() at call sites in main.rs:62,68).

findings.description: WorkHour.member_id is typed as Option<serde_json::Value> because Teable returns either a linked-record object {"id": ...} or a plain string. All consumers must call the ad-hoc get_member_id() parser (lines 231-244) which re-implements deserialization at every use site.
findings.fix: Introduce a typed representation, e.g. '#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(untagged)] enum LinkedRecord { Object { id: String }, Plain(String) }' with a method as_id(&self) -> &str, and change the field to 'pub member_id: Option<LinkedRecord>'. Then simplify get_member_id() to self.member_id.as_ref().map(LinkedRecord::as_id) or remove it in favor of direct field access.

findings.description: get_work_hours_for_member_at_date() returns Result<Vec<serde_json::Value>> - raw untyped JSON leaks across the API boundary; the caller in routes/work_hours.rs only checks .is_empty(), so the Values are never meaningfully used.
findings.fix: Either narrow the API to what is actually needed - e.g. 'async fn work_hour_exists_for_member_at_date(...) -> Result<bool>' performing the request and returning !records.is_empty() - or return Vec<WorkHour> via the existing typed parsing.

findings.description: Every authenticated request logs two info! lines (utils.rs:93 'Verifying token', utils.rs:97 'Token valid'), and every Teable call logs the full URL (teable.rs:152) plus response size (teable.rs:182) at info level. On hot paths this floods logs and adds formatting cost per request.
findings.fix: Demote these four call sites from info! to debug! (keep warn!/error! for failures). Auth verification success and per-request URLs are diagnostic detail, not operational signal.

findings.description: Old numeric user IDs are detected via 'claims.sub == "0" || claims.sub.parse::<u32>().is_ok()' - a magic heuristic whose intent (reject pre-Teable numeric IDs, accept 'rec...' IDs) is undocumented in code and relies on parse failure side-effects.
findings.fix: Replace with an explicit, commented check, e.g. 'let is_legacy_numeric_id = claims.sub.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit());' and reject when true, with a comment stating Teable record IDs start with 'rec' and are never all-digits.

findings.description: Test env setup is copy-pasted: 54 std::env::set_var calls appear across ~10 test functions (first block at 293-316 inside create_test_app_with_teable_url, then repeated manually e.g. lines ~894-906, ~958-970, ~1279-1290, ~1396-1408). Tests also mutate process-global env, relying on serial_test to avoid races.
findings.fix: Extract one 'fn set_test_env(teable_url: &str)' helper containing the full set_var block; call it from create_test_app_with_teable_url and from every test that currently re-sets variables manually. Longer-term, refactor Config/TeableConfig to be passed through AppState (see finding B) so tests construct configs directly instead of mutating env.

findings.description: Stale #[allow(dead_code)] attributes: RegisterRequest (line 24) and ResetPasswordRequest (line 37) ARE constructed by axum's Json extractor in routes/auth.rs, so the suppression is wrong. SendTestMailRequest (52) and SendBulkMailRequest (67) are pub items exported via specta; the dead_code lint does not fire on pub items, so these suppressions are unnecessary too.
findings.fix: Delete all four struct-level #[allow(dead_code)] attributes (keep the field-level ones on WorkHour at lines 213-219 where fields are genuinely deserialized-but-unread).

findings.description: register() ignores its payload and returns {"message": "Registrierung erfolgreich"} with success semantics while creating nothing. Clients receive a fake success for a no-op.
findings.fix: Either implement registration or make the stub honest: return StatusCode::NOT_IMPLEMENTED (501) with a JSON body explaining registration is disabled (e.g. managed externally in Teable).

findings.description: The application uses the default system allocator and compiles for the generic x86-64 baseline. The guidelines recommend mimalloc as global allocator (measured up to 25% on alloc-hot paths) and the highest deployment-safe target-cpu.
findings.fix: Add 'mimalloc = "0.1"' to Cargo.toml [dependencies] and '#[global_allocator] static GLOBAL: mimalloc::MiMalloc = mimalloc::MiMalloc;' in main.rs. Optionally add backend/.cargo/config.toml with target-cpu=x86-64-v3 for the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu target (verify the Docker/CI base image supports v3 first).

findings.description: main.rs declares 'mod auth; mod config; ... mod utils;' (lines 22-32) that duplicate the pub mod declarations in lib.rs (lines 4-12). The same source files are compiled into two separate module trees (binary crate and library crate), so types like crate::auth::AuthClaims vs tsv_tennis_backend::auth::AuthClaims are distinct types - a classic source of confusing mismatch errors.
findings.fix: In main.rs, remove the duplicated 'mod' declarations for modules exported by lib.rs (auth, config, database, email, member_selection, models, teable, token_store, utils); keep only binary-local modules (mod routes; mod state;). Change main.rs imports from 'crate::config::Config' to 'tsv_tennis_backend::config::Config' (and likewise in state.rs, routes/*.rs). Verify with cargo build + cargo test.
